title: Execution corridor OKR hypotheses + All-Hands slate (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working draft for the cross-company Q3 planning cycle: a compact set of OKR hypotheses (execution corridors) + a lightweight All-Hands slate to align messaging and asks. Use this as the input for leadership review (3/12) and the cross-team prioritization forum (3/14).

Context / framing notes (short):
- We need a narrower set of measurable targets for the next 90 days that intentionally trade breadth for clear delivery corridors.
- Aim: reduce sprint collision between Serving Runtime, Dedicated & Private onboarding, and Console rollouts.
- Primary audience: Execs + Eng leads + Product managers who will commit to owner-level deliverables.
- This is intentionally a hypothesis deck — expect changes after the cross-team prioritization session.

High-level outcomes we want (qual + quant):
1) Latency reliability: 99th percentile inference latency under 1100ms for hosted-critical models at 95% load (baseline: 1250ms)
2) Cost/unit reduction: 15% net per-token compute cost on common gen workloads via batching/quantization + runtime tweaks
3) Onboarding throughput: shorten Dedicated and Private deployment time-to-first-inference from 5 days -> 3 days for standard templates
4) Developer velocity: reduce end-to-end incident-to-rollout time by 35% via console-driven rollouts + tracing playbooks

Proposed OKR hypotheses (90-day, owner-level)
OKR A — Serving Runtime performance corridor (owner: Sanjay Rao)
- O: Improve token-level throughput and tail latency for mid-sized seq lengths (512)
- KR1: 99th pct latency drop from 1250ms -> <=1100ms on 95% of production traffic (measurement: prod traces, label: model-family-core)
- KR2: Increase continuous-batch efficiency such that tokens/sec per-GPU improves by +12% on benchmark suite (suite v2)
- KR3: Reduce variance of model hot-swap path (fallbacks) so automatic fallback success rate >= 98%

OKR B — Cost & Optimize toolkit rollout (owner: Aisha Patel)
- O: Deliver first-pass Optimize recommendations for top-20 customers and pipeline to apply them safely
- KR1: Ship Optimize UI + automated suggestion engine (alpha) to Console with 3 rule types (batching, cache, quant profile)
- KR2: Implement A/B pilot with 5 customers, achieve median cost reduction >= 10% without measurable quality drop (eval prompt set)
- KR3: Publish internal runbook for opt-in automation + rollback patterns

OKR C — Dedicated & Private onboarding velocity (owner: Marco Liu)
- O: Make dedicated/private onboarding predictable and template-driven
- KR1: Create and ship 3 production-ready deck templates (SaaS, Regulated, Data-sensitive) and one-click infra bootstrap
- KR2: Cut mean time-to-first-inference for template installs from 5d -> 3d (metrics captured in onboarding sheet)
- KR3: Add KMS/HSM validation checks into onboarding pipeline; false-positive rate < 2%

OKR D — Console & Rollouts (owner: Ethan Brooks)
- O: Make rollout controls the default path for at-risk deploys
- KR1: Canary pipeline adoption >= 60% of internal deploys (tracked by route tag)
- KR2: Per-route observability dashboard templating shipped and adopted by 4 product teams
- KR3: Incident-to-rollback median time <= 8 minutes with playbook + one-click rollback

Dependencies / cross-team notes:
- Serving-runtime: needs kernel-selection tuning and a focused perf lab window (Sanjay + infra)
- Console: needs UI slots and an API for Optimize suggestions (Ethan + DevX)
- Sales/CS: must pre-approve pilot customer list (Maya / CS)
- Security: KMS/HSM onboarding checks need sign-off (legal/security)

Risk register (top 6 quick points):
- Risk 1: Performance regressions from quantization profiles -> mitigate: gated experiments + canaries
- Risk 2: Customer friction with auto-apply suggestions -> mitigate: manual opt-in + rollback + customer comms templates
- Risk 3: Deployment windows collide with infra maintenance -> mitigate: ops blockade windows + prioritize critical canaries
- Risk 4: Underestimated integration work for Private (networking/KMS) -> mitigate: separate minimal-viable-private checklist
- Risk 5: Metrics noise (A/B) -> mitigate: baked-in evaluation prompt sets and quality thresholds
- Risk 6: Exec ask overload (scope creep) -> mitigate: team-level refusal gates and explicit deprioritization list

All-Hands slate (proposed, 20–25 min total)
- 0:00–2:00 — Quick CEO 1-min framing: why tighter corridors now
- 2:00–8:00 — Exec update (ops + product): Big bets and tradeoffs (Claire + Sanjay)
- 8:00–14:00 — What we shipped recently (2 quick wins): Dedicated templates + Optimize alpha (Aisha)
- 14:00–18:00 — Road ahead (90-day corridors & top 4 asks) (Claire)
- 18:00–22:00 — Cross-functional ask: Where we need help (2–3 asks per function: SRE, Sales, Security)
- 22:00–25:00 — Live Q&A + CTA: sign up for squad pledges + follow-up channels

Comms + pre-reads (deliverables before All-Hands):
- 1-pager: 90-day corridor summary (this doc distilled) — owner: Claire — due 3/17
- Tech note: perf lab plan and canary runbook — owner: Sanjay — due 3/18
- Pilot comms: customer-facing guidance for Optimize pilots — owner: Aisha/Maya — due 3/18
- Internal signup form (squad pledges) — owner: People Ops — due 3/16

Meeting ask checklist for leadership review (3/12):
- Review & sign off on top-line KRs for each owner (Sanjay, Aisha, Marco, Ethan)
- Confirm the 5 pilot customers for Optimize A/B (Maya)
- Approve the All-Hands agenda and identify up to two exec talking points
- Confirm a shared measurement dashboard and owner (infra metrics owner TBD)

Open questions / things to decide quickly:
- Q1: Are we comfortable with the latency SLO target (1100ms 99th) as a company-level ask or restrict to hosted-api only?
- Q2: Should Optimize suggestions be default opt-out or opt-in for pilot customers?
- Q3: Do we want to shift one Dedicated engineering squad from new features -> onboarding acceleration for the quarter?

Quick next steps (this week):
- 3/11: Collate feedback from weekly eng leads (Claire)
- 3/12: Leadership review (30m) — goal: sign off on owners and top-line KRs
- 3/13: Product-ops + CS sync to finalize pilot customer list
- 3/14: Cross-team prioritization forum — finalize commitments and blockade windows

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally tight. Please call out any KR that feels impossible vs. aspirational.
- If you add a KR, please add a measurable metric and an owner. No unlabeled commitments.
- Link any related tickets with the standard prefix JIRA-OPS- or PR links so we can stitch dashboards.

Footer:
Draft authored by Claire Nguyen (product-ops). Latest edit: 2025-03-11. Please use inline comments on this doc and ping me on #company-ops for urgent items.
